eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.2:_: (2) [Levush] Above siman 193 etc. Malbushei Yom Tov wrote it is not there because of general obligation; and on the contrary below siman 479 it is proven that specifically on Passover nights one must return after three; but Rosh's words in chapter "three who ate" that if one comes one must give him—and therefore it is not difficult against him, for in chapter Arvei Pesachim he ruled that even on Passover nights they do not have the custom to return after three—until here. And I did not know what difficulty he has on Levush, for there is no doubt that instead of siman 192 one should say siman 193, for in seif 1 it is explained there like Levush that they must return after zimun; and what he challenged from siman 479—it seems to me it is no difficulty at all, for there it teaches us it is a mitzvah to return after zimun to answer Hodu, and the practical difference is they should not separate after birkat hamazon; or even if he had no obligation to bless birkat hamazon, nevertheless he returns after zimun to answer Hodu. One can also say that what Levush wrote—mitzvah to return after three—and indeed in Ma'adanei Melech there he wrote: one could say that in chapter Arvei Pesachim he proved there is no mitzvah to return after three except on Passover nights, and even on Passover night he concludes they did not have this custom—until here his language. And in any case we see Malbushei Yom Tov resolves this wonder that I brought, and it is reasonable to him that the same law applies—if three come to him he must return after him that he eat and invite zimun with him. It also seems to me to resolve the main wonder of Ma'adanei Melech on Rosh and his difficulty on Levush—that on Passover night even if one eats he must return after zimun, unlike other days of the year when one is obligated only when they are two, as above siman 193—and understand well. And in the essence of this law I am uncertain, and ostensibly it implies in the Talmud [Berachot] 47 that from Shmuel's statement "if they would bring me ardilia and gozalia to eat" etc.—one alone does not suffice but we require both. And if so, even if one says "hav lan venevarekh" or washed hands and the second intends to eat more, the third does not join with them; but in poskim it somewhat implies that even when one's mind is to eat more he combines—and per this one must say Shmuel stated the straightforward truth, and it requires study.
eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.3:_: (3) They said "hav" etc. And the same applies when he took the cup to bless even if they did not say "hav lan" etc., as above siman 179 seif 3. But it is difficult why Shulchan Aruch and Levush ruled here without qualification, and in siman 179 seif 1 they wrote that per R' Yitzchak and Ran it is permitted to eat without a blessing even if they said "hav lan venevarekh"—and if so here too he combines.
eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.4:_: (4) [Levush] Or even etc. Malbushei Yom Tov wrote: what is "even"—one need not say it, as above at the beginning of siman 179—until here. And in the remainder of Kenesset HaGedolah the Beit Yosef wondered at Rama who wrote that washing mayim acharonim is like "hav lan," for it is inferior to "hav lan"; and see above siman 101 where I wrote in the name of Rashba that "hav lan" is inferior to mayim acharonim; and if so one can say Rama means that in this law everyone agrees they are equal. It also seems to my humble opinion to resolve that it is reasonable to him as Bach wrote—that even when they say "hav lan venevarekh" it is a mitzvah they return to eat and wash hands and bless haMotzi so they may invite zimun with him; and therefore he wrote mayim acharonim is like "hav lan," for even though he ruled in siman 179 it is forbidden to eat after mayim acharonim even if he washes and blesses, nevertheless here because of the mitzvah of zimun one may rely on poskim who permit; and see there what I brought that they are permitted to eat even if not for zimun's sake. And in any case the essence of this law Bach wrote—mitzvah to return and eat—and so wrote Magen Avraham—is not clear to me, for I did not find a root for this; and it implies in Talmud and poskim this is a completely separate eating since he must bless before it; and if they eat more and invite zimun it is as if they eat anew and invite; and so implies Derishah—and see above siman 193 s.k. 10.

kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.1:_: (1) [Seif 1] Two who ate as one and finished etc.—the same applies to one who ate and finished and afterward two came who can invite zimun. Maamar Mordechai ot 1; and nevertheless there is no obligation unless they wait until they eat and invite—unless they are two who ate as one and finished and afterward a third came, as written in Shulchan Aruch.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.2:_: (2) [Seif 1] Wherever if they would bring him something etc.—even dessert such as greens and mushrooms and fowl. Gemara. Magen Avraham s.k. 1. And even if they cannot eat anything at all. R' Zalman ot 1.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.3:_: (3) There—they can eat from it etc.—even though they ate nothing since he came to them. R' Zalman there. And even if that food is not before him, nevertheless we say: if it were before him he would eat. Derishah ot 1; and what is written there on Levush—see Eliyah Rabbah ot 1 who resolves—see there.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.4:_: (4) There—and they must give him etc.—because it is a mitzvah they return after a third that he join them for zimun, as written above siman 193 seif 1; and that which is stated below siman 479—mitzvah to return after zimun on Passover nights—which implies on other days of the year there is no mitzvah and no obligation—one can say there one must invite for zimun from before the meal; but here specifically if it occurred during the meal they must give him so he may join. Maamar Mordechai ot 3.

levushei-serad/part-001.txt.1:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 2—for Ran he combines; Ran's view in Mechaber there seif 1 that even if they said "hav venevarekh" they may eat without a blessing—if so they are still within "they can eat" and combine; and Shulchan Aruch ruled that here it is per one view there that if they wish to eat after saying "hav lan venevarekh" they must bless haMotzi—automatically this is not called "they can eat," for when he eats another meal he will eat.
levushei-serad/part-001.txt.2:_: s.k. 3—mayim acharonim is preferable, meaning regarding if they wish to eat after mayim acharonim; Mechaber ruled siman 179 that even haMotzi does not help but he must begin with birkat hamazon—unlike "hav lan venevarekh" where for everyone haMotzi suffices; behold mayim acharonim is preferable; and if so what does Rama teach us—behold all the more so.
levushei-serad/part-001.txt.3:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 5—and nevertheless he requires a measure: meaning a kazayit; and it is difficult—for if there is a kazayit what difference does dipping make, for without dipping he combines because of the kazayit he ate; and one can say we hold vegetable and brine combine to a kazayit—so too Peri Megadim in the name of Levush.
levushei-serad/part-001.txt.4:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 7—he is discharged by Borei nefashot rabot—wine too one does zimun; thus is the reading.

machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.1:_: (s.k. 1) They can etc.—even dessert etc. And Levush wrote: specifically when he is not disgusted by the food; and so implies Shulchan Aruch's wording.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.2:_: He came etc.—for Ran he combines etc.; Ran holds that even if they say "hav lan venevarekh" specifically to drink it is forbidden, but to eat it is permitted and he need not bless on it; if so even if they said "hav lan" etc. it is not departure, for he is still permitted to eat.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.3:א: (s.k. 3) And washing etc.—as written there in siman 179 that although Ran holds with "hav lan venevarekh" one may eat, but with washing hands he concedes to Rosh it is forbidden to eat.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.3:ב: And it appears to me he came to teach us etc.—meaning on the contrary—what Rama wrote "and washing etc. like hav lan" means a leniency: that also with mayim acharonim you find they combine, as with "hav lan"—meaning if he wishes to bless first even though it is forbidden etc.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.3:ג: But he must bless birkat hamazon first—for one can say they are always permitted, as Magen Avraham wrote in siman 179, not like Rabbeinu Yehudah there.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.4:_: (s.k. 4) They combine etc.—and it is not similar to siman 194, for if one of the three who ate together blessed birkat hamazon by himself, nevertheless the two invite zimun with him.

magen-avraham/part-001.txt.1:א: They can eat. Even dessert such as greens and mushrooms and fowl (gemara).
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.1:ב: The third came. And see siman 179 that per Ran he combines—all who have not washed hands.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.1:ג: And washing etc. And it requires study, for on the contrary mayim acharonim is preferable as written there; and one must say he came to teach us that if he wishes to bless and eat they are permitted even though they forbid doing so as written siman 179—nevertheless here because of the mitzvah of zimun they are permitted, for some hold they are always permitted to eat with a blessing as written there; and Bach wrote that here it is a mitzvah they wash hands and bless haMotzi and eat a little—and so is primary.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.2:א: They combine. And if he already recited the final blessing he cannot again invite zimun with them for he already departed from them (Hagahot Agudah); and some say for siman 194 seif 1 that there at least he ate bread.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.2:ב: In brine. And nevertheless we require a measure.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.2:ג: Except water. Because one does not do zimun, as Rashi explained in the first chapter of Eruvin (Beit Yosef); and it requires study, for nevertheless he can say "who has fed us from His bounty," for even drinking water is included in eating, as in Yoreh Deah siman 238 seif 2; and Tosafot wrote the reason is because drinking is included in eating, and even though in the gemara it mentions a cup of wine, nevertheless it is not specific, for there are other beverages—but it mentions wine to teach that even so he does not discharge others—see there; and also all poskim wrote generically "who drank"—therefore it seems he combines.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.3:א: And he is not discharged. For even the bread-eater, if he ate one thing after the meal he must bless on it, as written siman 178—all the more so this one who did not eat bread at all; and if he drank wine it implies in Beit Yosef in the name of Rashba he is discharged from Borei nefashot rabot—wine too one does zimun; and see siman 208 seif 17 that the same applies to dates; nevertheless l'chatchila he should intend not to be discharged by Borei nefashot rabot, for he must bless on every species fitting for him.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.3:ב: With vegetables etc. And specifically a kazayit.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.3:ג: To drink. And so Bach wrote his rabbis were accustomed to give him to drink if he did not want to eat and he combines; and so is the custom now.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.4:א: Mitzvah that he bless. For from Torah he is not obligated to bless unless he ate to satiety; and as Beit Yosef—that if each blesses to himself in a whisper and only they invite zimun, even one who ate a kazayit can bless; and see siman 183 seif 7.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.4:ב: He can discharge. For from Torah he can discharge his fellow even though he did not eat, since his fellow already ate and is obligated to bless, and all Israel are guarantors for one another—as written end of siman 196; except he cannot say "who has fed us" unless he ate a kazayit (Tosafot, Beit Yosef); and Ateret Zekenim did not look in Beit Yosef, and it ostensibly implies if they are two he need not say "who has fed us"—he can discharge his fellow even though he did not eat; and nevertheless in beginning of siman 193 it implies he does not discharge his fellow unless he ate—and so in Tosafot in the name of Yerushalmi.
magen-avraham/part-001.txt.4:ג: And some say he is not obligated. And per their words, if he ate a kazayit he is obligated d'oraisa to bless; and per Rabbeinu Yehudah it is only d'rabbanan, for that which we expound "and you shall eat"—eating measure of a kazayit—is merely an asmakhta, for d'oraisa we require actual satiety; and so say most poskim, and Bach did not understand Rabbeinu Yehudah's words on this—see there; and if some ate to satiety and did not drink, and some did not eat to satiety and drank—it is better they bless over those who ate to satiety, for they are obligated d'oraisa per most poskim, for we are not concerned with drinking; and see end of siman 186. One who eats coarse eating discharges others in birkat hamazon if his throat enjoyed that eating (Shulchan Gavoah chapter 7); see siman 602 seif 6.

mechaber/part-001.txt.1:main: The laws of joining for zimun of three or ten. And it contains 4 seifim: Two who ate as one and finished, and a third came—wherever if they would bring him something they could still eat from it, he joins with them, and they are obligated to give him to eat so he may join with them; and this is when he came before they said "give us and let us bless"; but if they said "give us and let us bless" and afterward the third came, he does not join with them. {Rama: And washing mayim acharonim is like "give us and let us bless" (Mordechai chapter "three who ate"). And see above siman 179.}
mechaber/part-001.txt.2:main: Nine who ate grain and one ate a kazayit of vegetable—they combine to mention the Name, even if he only dipped with them in brine, or only drank with them one cup containing a revi'it of any beverage except water—he joins with them, provided the one blessing is one of the bread-eaters; and even if seven ate grain and three ate vegetable they combine; but six do not, for we require a recognizable majority.
mechaber/part-001.txt.3:main: The one who joins must bless the final blessing on what he ate and is not discharged by their birkat hamazon. In what case? That any food suffices to join for ten; but for three he does not join until he eats a kazayit of bread; some say a kazayit of grain even if not bread; some say vegetables or any food. Therefore two who ate and a third came—if they can induce him to eat a kazayit of bread it is better; if he does not want they should not give him to drink or other food; but if they gave him to drink or other food they invite zimun with him even if he does not want to eat bread.
mechaber/part-001.txt.4:main: Companions who ate together—some ate to satiety and some only a kazayit—if all know how to bless, it is a mitzvah that one who ate to satiety bless and discharge the others; if not all know, one who ate a kazayit can discharge even those who ate to satiety. {Rama: And some say he is not obligated from the Torah if he did not drink and is thirsty to drink (Mordechai chapter "three who ate," Beit Yosef in the name of Kol Bo and Shibolei Leket). And it is good to be careful l'chatchila: if some drank and some did not, that one who drank blesses (his own words).}

mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:א: (1) And a third came—and wishes to eat and join them for zimun.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:ב: (2) They can eat from it—meaning they are not so satiated that if they brought them things that sustain the heart for dessert of the meal, such as fruits and greens and mushrooms and young pigeons and the like, they could eat—even a little of them.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:ג: (3) He joins with them—for we consider them as if they have not yet finished their meal, and this is when he fixed with them—meaning he ate with them at the table where they sit, as written in siman 193 seif 2—see there in Mishna Berurah. Ma'amar Mordechai wrote the same applies if one finished his meal at first and afterward two came to him and eat—he also joins with them for zimun if they would bring him something and he can eat from it—see there; he also wrote the same in all this for joining ten to mention the Name.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:ד: (4) And they must give etc.—not specifically, but he meant it is a mitzvah to give him, as he wrote above at the beginning of siman 193.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:ה: (5) He does not join with them—for since they said so they already diverted their minds from eating and drinking, and it is forbidden for them to eat again as explained above in siman 179 seif 1 per the first view—and therefore he cannot join with them, for they already departed from their first eating; and see Biur Halacha.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:ו: (6) And see above siman 179—for there the details of the laws of "hav lan venevarekh" and mayim acharonim were explained.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.2:א: (7) And one ate etc.—for although on vegetables one does not bless birkat hamazon, nevertheless he can combine and answer "Blessed are You... who has fed us from His bounty."
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.2:ב: (8) Kazayit of vegetable—its reason: since he says "who has fed us" and there is no eating less than a kazayit; or because we require he be obligated in some blessing, and with less than a kazayit there is no obligation in any blessing after his eating, as explained below siman 210.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.2:ג: (9) They combine—and if he already blessed the final blessing they cannot again invite zimun upon him, for he already departed from them [Magen Avraham and Sha'arei Teshuvah].
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.2:ד: (10) In brine—meaning he dipped vegetable in brine, and among all of them there was only a kazayit—nevertheless he combines.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.2:ה: (11) One cup—for drinking is included in eating and he can say "who has fed us."
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.2:ו: (12) Except water—for water does not do zimun and it is not considered for joining, even if he is thirsty and wishes to drink; and Magen Avraham disagrees and ruled he combines, for all drinking is included in eating—and some Acharonim brought this for the law; however in Bigdei Yeshu'a and Magen Giborim they agreed with the Mechaber, and so sides Chemed Moshe.
